scenario: [LTIM.8.2.3] / [LTIM.8.2.4]: the exact `iso8601` text `::String` writes ([LCST.4.5.9]), compared character for character. A `Time` read from a slot is UTC ([LTIM.1.1.3]), so its zone is `Z`. The fraction is written only when the sub-second part is not zero, as nine digits with the trailing zeros removed: 1700000000 s is `2023-11-14T22:13:20Z`; one nanosecond more is `.000000001`; 500 ms is `.5`; 123456780 ns is `.12345678`; one nanosecond before the epoch floors to `1969-12-31T23:59:59.999999999Z`. A `Date` is `YYYY-MM-DD`, at the epoch, a day either side of it, and at both ends of [LTIM.1.2.2]'s range. A `Time` at a non-zero offset (`+hh:mm`, `-hh:mm`) needs `local()` and a `TimeZoneOffset` row for its zone ([LTIM.10.7]), which this vector does not assert; each runtime's unit suite pins it (libds `test_rete_time.c`, Mercury `test_ds`). Pin: five lines in assert order. A writer that always wrote nine digits, dropped the fraction, wrote `+00:00` for UTC, or truncated a negative instant toward zero gives a different line. PATH PINNED: FN_TO_STRING in libds's `fmt_iso8601` / `fmt_date` (rete/adapters.c) and Mercury's `ds.format.render_iso8601` / `ds.eval.ltim_8_2_1_render_date`.
